chase_cards.name: Misdreavus [Pokémon Card Trainers Vol. 9]
chase_cards.why: This is a chase because it is a small ghost routed through a specialist magazine: a Johto-era atmosphere card with Awakening Legends bones, English Neo memory, and a species built around fear as energy.

key_artists.name: Shin-ichi Yoshida
key_artists.why: Yoshida matters here because Misdreavus is a mood card: the illustrator credit keeps the visual atmosphere attached to the exact magazine promo route instead of letting later English Neo memory flatten it.

claims.text: The local catalog models the Pokémon Card Trainers Vol. 9 insert source group as one row containing Misdreavus at source index 219.
Bulbapedia places the Japanese Misdreavus print in Unnumbered Promotional cards and identifies its release as a Pokémon Card Trainers Vol. 9 insert on December 1, 2000.
Bulbapedia identifies the Japanese promo as ムウマ Misdreavus, a Psychic-type Basic Pokémon card with 60 HP, Pain Split, and Confuse Ray.
Bulbapedia credits the Misdreavus artwork to Shin-ichi Yoshida.
Bulbapedia says the Japanese print includes the Awakening Legends symbol and border text, while the English print appeared in Neo Revelation.
Bulbapedia's Shin-ichi Yoshida category includes multiple Japanese-era cards, making the artist credit useful as a sourced art trace but not a substitute for release-route proof.

Bulbapedia's Misdreavus species page describes it as a Generation II Ghost-type Pokémon that startles people at night, uses its red orbs to absorb fear, and may yank or bite at hair to generate reactions.

As judged collector texture, Trainers Vol. 9 Misdreavus matters because the release route and the species mood line up: a quiet magazine insert for a ghost Pokémon whose whole identity is atmosphere, fear, and sudden attention.

narrative.human_title: Pokémon Card Trainers Vol. 9 Misdreavus: a ghost in the magazine lane
narrative.why_it_matters: Misdreavus is exactly the sort of card that disappears if the catalog only knows set names. It is a Japanese Trainers Vol. 9 insert with Awakening Legends text in its bones, an English Neo Revelation afterimage, and a Johto ghost identity built around fear, night, and sudden attention. The card feels like a small haunting in the release map: quiet, specific, and easy to misfile unless the route stays attached.
